summary: This note is a short stub about SM UB-27, a German Type UB II submarine (U-boat) of the German Imperial Navy during World War I. It gives the boat's ordering, launch and commissioning dates in 1915 and 1916. It also states that UB-27 sank 11 ships in 17 patrols, but the tonnage total is missing from the note.
one_line: SM UB-27 was a German Type UB II U-boat of the Imperial Navy in World War I, sinking 11 ships in 17 patrols.
key_facts: SM UB-27 was a German Type UB II submarine, also called a U-boat, in the German Imperial Navy during World War I.
SM UB-27 was ordered on 30 April 1915.
SM UB-27 was launched on 10 February 1916.
SM UB-27 was commissioned into the German Imperial Navy on 23 February 1916.
SM UB-27 sank 11 ships in 17 patrols.
The note gives the total tonnage sunk by SM UB-27 as blank, so the figure is not recorded.
The designation SM stands for Seiner Majestät (His Majesty's), as the note uses the prefix SM for the boat's name.
The note belongs to a series of wiki entries on German U-boats of World War I.
